title: Property Rights
summary: The right to keep and use the product of your effort, and why freedom of action requires it.

lessons.title: What property is
lessons.objective: Name property as the right to keep and use the product of your effort.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what is a property right?

choices.text: The right to keep and use the product of your effort
A duty to split every gain with the group
A title the state may invent without your work
A feeling that something ought to be yours

feedback.note: Property, here, is the right to keep and use what your effort produces. It is not a mood, a group split, or a title with no work behind it.

exercises.prompt: Which two acts does the right cover?

choices.text: Keeping the product and using it
Looking at it but never using it
Handing it over as soon as it is made
Voting on who may keep it next

feedback.note: The right is not bare display. It is the right to keep the product and to use it.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to the idea it names.

pairs.left: Property right
pairs.right: Keep and use the product of your effort

pairs.left: What the right covers
What the right is not
pairs.right: A feeling that something ought to be yours

feedback.note: Name the right by what it covers: keep and use the product of your effort. A feeling is not the right.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit's name for the right.

parts.text: A property right is the right to keep and

feedback.note: The missing act is use. Surrender, display, and a vote are not the name of the right.

exercises.prompt: Build the study sentence.

feedback.note: Call property a right to keep. A mood is not that right. The extra word a does not belong in the sentence.

exercises.prompt: A farmer grows a crop by his own work. Under this unit, the crop is what?

choices.text: The product of his effort, which he has a right to keep and use
Nobody's until a committee names an owner
Automatically everyone's, because food is useful
A gift of the soil, so his work does not matter

feedback.note: The crop is the product of his effort. The right is to keep it and use it. Usefulness to others does not erase that.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to how this unit treats it.

pairs.left: Wages you earned
pairs.right: A product you may keep and use

pairs.left: A wish to own a neighbor's tools
The two acts in the right

feedback.note: Earned wages fit the right. A wish for someone else's tools does not. The acts are keep and use.

exercises.prompt: Fill both blanks from the unit summary.

parts.text: and use the product of your

feedback.note: Keep names the holding. Effort names whose product it is. Borrow and luck are not the claim.

exercises.prompt: Which statement matches this lesson?

choices.text: Property is the right to keep and use the product of your effort
Property is only a paper label with no right to use
Property is whatever you can take and hold by strength
Property is assigned by who needs the thing most

feedback.note: This lesson only names the right. Taking by strength and assigning by need are different claims, and a label without use is too thin.

lessons.title: The product of your effort
lessons.objective: Identify what the right covers as the product of your own effort, and reject treating another person's product as yours.

exercises.prompt: What does the property right cover?

choices.text: The product of your own effort
The product of anyone whose work you admire
Goods that appear with no effort at all
A common pool of everyone's products

feedback.note: The right tracks your effort. It does not cover another person's product or a pool of everyone's goods.

exercises.prompt: You did not make, earn, or trade for a tool. Under this unit, is it your property?

choices.text: No. It is not the product of your effort
Yes, if you want it more than the maker does
Yes, if the tool is useful to many people
Yes, after you have looked at it long enough

feedback.note: Wanting a thing, or its being useful, does not make it the product of your effort.

exercises.prompt: Match each case to the right verdict.

pairs.left: Pay you earned this week
A neighbor's harvest you did not grow
A book you wrote
A book someone else wrote
pairs.right: The writer's product, not yours by wanting it

feedback.note: The line is whose effort produced it. Your pay and your book fall on your side. Their harvest and their book do not.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast.

parts.text: The right covers the product of

feedback.note: Your effort sets the coverage. Another person's effort stays outside it. Nobody and every erase that line.

exercises.prompt: Build the study sentence.

feedback.note: The product of your effort is yours. It is not automatically everyone's, and the claim is not optional wording.

exercises.prompt: A trader swaps goods both sides produced or already owned by honest trade. What is that swap?

choices.text: Each side using and disposing of his own product
Each side taking the other's product without right
A cancellation of property, because goods moved
A public assignment of both products

feedback.note: Trade is a use of what is already yours. Moving goods by agreement does not make them a common pool.

exercises.prompt: Match the mistake to why it fails.

pairs.left: I need it, so it is mine
We all benefit, so it is ours
pairs.right: A benefit is not a claim on the maker's product

pairs.left: I could have made it, so I own it
pairs.right: Possible effort is not the effort that produced it

feedback.note: Need, a shared benefit, and effort you did not do are not the product of your effort.

exercises.prompt: Build the rejection.

feedback.note: Another person's product is not yours. Always and shared would erase the line this lesson draws.

exercises.prompt: Which line keeps this lesson's point?

choices.text: Your effort's product is yours; another person's product is not
Every useful thing belongs to whoever can use it
Nothing produced can be owned, because nature supplied the materials
Half of every product belongs to people who did not make it

feedback.note: Materials from nature do not cancel the effort that turned them into a product. The right still follows that effort, not a forced half-share.

lessons.title: The right to use it
lessons.objective: Treat use as part of the right, and reject a title that forbids the owner to act on what he keeps.

exercises.prompt: You may keep a workshop, but you are forbidden to run it, sell from it, or alter it. What is missing?

choices.text: The right to use the product of your effort
A longer name on the deed
A crowd to approve each tool
A rule that the building is nobody's

feedback.note: Keeping without use is not the right this unit names. The missing part is use.

exercises.prompt: Which control counts as use in this lesson?

choices.text: Acting on what you keep: employing it, consuming it, or trading it
Only being allowed to look at it
Asking permission every time you touch your own product
Waiting until others have used it first

feedback.note: Use means you may act on the product: employ it, consume it, or trade it. Looking, and waiting for others, are not that use.

exercises.prompt: Match each setup to the verdict.

pairs.left: You own the press and may print with it
You hold title but may not operate the press
pairs.right: Keep without the right of use

pairs.left: Someone else runs your press by your agreement

feedback.note: Use can be your own hands or a use you chose, including a trade. A ban on operating what you keep cuts the right.

exercises.prompt: Complete the lesson's contrast.

parts.text: A title you cannot act on is not the full right, because the right includes

feedback.note: The word is use. Display, silence, and a standing need for permission are not substitutes.

exercises.prompt: Build the study sentence.

feedback.note: The right includes use. Excludes would reverse the lesson. Guesswork is not part of the claim.

exercises.prompt: Selling what you made, because you choose to, is which of these?

choices.text: A use of your product
Proof that you never had a right to it
A ban on keeping anything
A start of force against the buyer

feedback.note: A chosen sale is a use. It does not erase the right, and an agreed trade is not force against the buyer.

exercises.prompt: Match each limit to what it does to the right.

pairs.left: You may not consume what you grew
You may not sell what you made
You may keep it only as a sealed exhibit

feedback.note: Barring consumption, sale, or any action leaves you with a label, not the right to use.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two acts the summary names.

parts.text: The right is to keep and

feedback.note: Use is the act. A label alone is the thin substitute this lesson rejects.

exercises.prompt: Which statement is the lesson's point?

choices.text: Property includes use; a title that forbids action is not the right
Property is only the paper, and use is a separate favor
You may use a thing once, then the right ends
Use belongs to others, and you only store the thing

feedback.note: Use is inside the right, not a favor, a one-time pass, or a job left to other people.

lessons.title: Why freedom of action requires it
lessons.objective: Explain that freedom of action requires property, because action needs control of its means and of its result.

exercises.prompt: Why does this unit say freedom of action requires property?

choices.text: Action needs control of its means and of its result
People prefer owning things, and tastes decide rights
Owners work faster, so the right is a growth trick
Most societies have used the word property

feedback.note: The reason is not taste, speed, or custom. Without control of means and result, the action is not yours to direct.

exercises.prompt: You may 'act freely,' but others seize whatever your action produces. What fails?

choices.text: Control of the result, so the freedom is empty
Only the spelling of the word freedom
Nothing, if you still feel free
Nothing, if a vote approved the seizure

feedback.note: If the result is taken, you do not control the action's product. A feeling or a vote does not restore that control.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of action to the control it needs.

pairs.left: The means you act with
pairs.right: Control so the tools of the action are yours to use

pairs.left: The result the action produces
pairs.right: Control so the product remains yours

pairs.left: Freedom of action without either control
pairs.right: A phrase with the action taken out of your hands

feedback.note: Means and result are the two controls. Drop both, and freedom of action is only a phrase.

exercises.prompt: Complete the reason.

parts.text: Freedom of action requires property because action needs control of its

feedback.note: The two words are means and result. An audience or a slogan is not what the action has to control.

exercises.prompt: Build the study sentence.

feedback.note: Freedom of action requires property. It does not replace property, and property is not decor.

exercises.prompt: Your tools are locked away from you, though you are told you may still 'choose your work.' What is blocked?

choices.text: Control of the means the action needs
Only the name of the trade
Nothing, because speech about work is still allowed
Only the weather, which property cannot touch

feedback.note: Without the means, the choice of work cannot be carried out. Speech about work is not control of the means.

exercises.prompt: Match the seizure to the control it breaks.

pairs.left: Your tools are taken before you work
Your finished goods are taken after you work
Both are left in your hands
pairs.right: The control freedom of action requires

feedback.note: Taking tools hits the means. Taking the finished goods hits the result. Leaving both is the control the freedom requires.

exercises.prompt: Build the reason in short form.

feedback.note: Read it as: no control of the result means no real freedom. Extra applause is not the reason.

exercises.prompt: Which statement is this lesson, and not a different unit?

choices.text: Freedom of action requires property, because action needs its means and its result
The lesson's job is to list police, courts, and defense
The lesson's job is to name laissez-faire as a system
The lesson's job is to define fraud as a start of force

feedback.note: This lesson is the link from freedom of action to property. Government's jobs, the name of capitalism, and the definition of force are other units.

exercises.prompt: If you control neither the means nor the result, what is left of 'freedom of action'?

choices.text: A permission to gesture, while the action's substance is out of your hands
Full freedom, because nobody argued with your opinions
More freedom, because nothing is yours to worry about
The same freedom as when you keep and use the product

feedback.note: Opinions without control of means and result are not the freedom of action this unit is protecting. Losing the product does not increase that freedom.

lessons.title: The whole claim
lessons.objective: Apply the full unit: the right to keep and use the product of your effort, because freedom of action requires that control.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence states the whole unit?

choices.text: You may keep and use the product of your effort, because freedom of action requires that control
You may look at your product, and others may use it
Freedom of action is whatever a vote leaves you this year
Effort creates no claim, and action needs no means

feedback.note: The whole claim joins keep, use, the product of your effort, and the reason: freedom of action requires that control.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the unit to its role.

pairs.left: Keep and use
Product of your effort
Freedom of action
Means and result

feedback.note: Acts, coverage, the freedom at stake, and the needed control are four parts of one claim.

exercises.prompt: A law lets you work but takes the product and locks the tools. Which parts of the unit does that break?

choices.text: Use of your means and keeping the result
None, if you are still called free
Only the spelling of property
Only your mood, which the right ignores

feedback.note: Locked tools deny use of the means. A taken product denies keeping the result. A flattering name does not repair either.

exercises.prompt: Complete the summary in the unit's words.

parts.text: and use the product of your effort, and why

feedback.note: Keep is the first act. Freedom of action is what requires the right. Charity and fashion are not the summary.

exercises.prompt: Build the whole claim in one line.

feedback.note: Keep and use what your effort produces. Abandon reverses the right. Anyone's would drop whose effort it was.

exercises.prompt: Someone says property is greed and freedom is doing without any means. What does this unit answer?

choices.text: Freedom of action requires control of means and result, which is the property right
Agree: the right is only a wish to have more than others
Drop use, and keep the word property as a courtesy
Swap the product to whoever has the stronger wish

feedback.note: The unit's answer is the requirement, not a contest of wishes and not a courtesy title.

exercises.prompt: Match each challenge to the part of the claim that answers it.

pairs.left: Why not take her product if I need it?
pairs.right: The right covers her effort, not your need

pairs.left: Why not let her keep it but ban her from using it?
Why does action care about ownership at all?
pairs.right: Without means and result, freedom of action is empty

feedback.note: Need does not move the product. A ban on use cuts the right. Action cares because it needs means and result.

exercises.prompt: Fill the chain.

parts.text: , and that is why freedom of action requires property.

feedback.note: Means, then result. A rumor or a permit is not the chain.

exercises.prompt: Build the reason that closes the unit.

feedback.note: Freedom of action requires that control. Cancels would deny the unit. Gossip is not a substitute for control.

exercises.prompt: A writer keeps her manuscript, revises it, and sells copies she chooses to sell. Which reading fits the unit?

choices.text: She keeps and uses the product of her effort, which her freedom of action requires
The sale proves the manuscript was never hers
Readers' wish to have it free overrides her effort
She may store the pages but must not revise or sell them

feedback.note: Keeping, revising, and a chosen sale are keep and use. Readers' wishes do not make the manuscript theirs, and a seal on use would cut the right.
